frontier.hypothesis: Target IS the 'p10 read below the Z0 store' regime -- that is the only regime in which the read has a RAW dep on the store and becomes ready in time -- and our bodies in that regime are 67 instructions where target is 66. The whole residual therefore reduces to a single un-diagnosed instruction of overhead in the below-store family, not to a scheduler tie.
frontier.mechanism: With the p10 read below the store, sched.c:1783 creates a true (RAW) memory dependence 12 <- 25 instead of the anti-dependence 25 <- 12, so uid 12 becomes ready before uid 25 is scheduled and can take target's slot. s24 killed the six below-store positions on SCORE (all 67 insns, score 5, one normalised cc1 stream) but never diagnosed WHERE the 67th instruction comes from -- and s25's zero-net-instruction budget constraint says that extra instruction is the entire remaining gap.
frontier.next_probe: Apply memory/grind/func_80060A68/rejected/s24-v2_p10_after_copy1-...-67insns.c (or regenerate X4 from tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s26/x/X4.c, score 5 / 67 insns), run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80060A68`, and diff its .cse/.combine/.sched dumps against the T1 dumps to name the pass that introduces the 67th instruction. Then diff the raw insn stream against target with tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s24/dumpdiff.py to identify WHICH instruction is extra. Removing that one instruction while keeping the below-store position closes the function; every other axis on this spine is now measured dead.

frontier.hypothesis: The only two unclosed routes through anti_dependence (sched.c:845-868) are memrefs_conflict_p returning 0 and the both-memrefs-volatile route; the former needs the p10 load's RTL base to be a SYMBOL_REF so find_symbolic_term succeeds on both sides at sched.c:697-705.
frontier.mechanism: memrefs_conflict_p reaches its distinct-symbolic-base branch only when both addresses are PLUS forms whose symbolic term can be found. Our p10 load's base is a pseudo holding the gp-loaded `outer` pointer; the Z0 store's base is the symbol D_800F10D0. If the p10 value could be read through an expression whose address RTL carries a symbol base (e.g. through a differently-declared global rather than through `outer`), the branch would compare two distinct symbols and return 0, deleting the anti-dep and putting uid 12 on the ready list at clock 44.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate the declared shapes of D_800A3468 and the +0x10 member in the DATA MODEL block of the brief and in include/*.h, and test whether any faithful spelling gives the p10 read a symbol-based address (it is read as *(s32 *)(D_800A3468 + 0x10), so the candidate is a spelling that keeps the symbol in the address rather than materialising `outer` first). Measure each with `sandbox func_80060A68 --disable all` and, before scoring, re-extract the model and check whether deps[25] still contains [12, 14] -- the dep, not the score, is the discriminator.

frontier.hypothesis: W1 (66 instructions, pure permutation of target's multiset) is the correct spine for a future solver session even though it scores 4, because it is the only body whose residual the sched_solver can express without an instruction-count change; its goal is `pick 12, then 15, then 31` after uid 33.
frontier.mechanism: tools/sched_solver models an exact permutation of an identical instruction multiset; T1 (65 insns) and E2 (66 insns but a different multiset) both require an insn to be added or removed, which no scheduler atom can express. W1's model is already extracted and validated (parity=True) and banked at tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s26/W1.sched.json.
frontier.next_probe: Run tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s24/run_perturb.py against tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s26/W1.sched.json with the goal stated MANUALLY as `--pass 2 --block 0 --goal-before 33:12 --goal-before 12:15 --goal-before 15:31` (goalmap cannot auto-derive it -- see evidence), depth 1 first, then depth 2 restricted to luid,luid_move.
